claims.text: A combined high-throughput DSC, CALPHAD, and MC/MD protocol can accurately determine melting temperature across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The combined protocol can accurately determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The combined protocol can accurately determine volume change on melting across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The combined protocol can accurately determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Combining high-throughput experiments and computation makes determination of these properties efficient.
Conventional synthesis can provide single-phase equimolar FCC or BCC HEA samples suitable for the protocol.
Controlled DSC captures the onset and progression of melting.
Coupling DSC with CALPHAD and MC/MD permits extraction of melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change.
Carefully calibrated heating rates control thermal gradients during high-temperature DSC measurements.
Atomic-scale complexity and configurational entropy in HEAs govern the balance of enthalpic and entropic contributions during melting.
The balance between enthalpy and entropy determines fusion properties, including melting temperature.
Chemical substitutions in HEAs alter both enthalpic stabilization and configurational entropy controlling melting.
DSC supplies a direct thermodynamic melting signature through endothermic peaks.
Third-generation thermodynamic descriptions and CALPHAD convert experimental signatures into accurate melting parameters.
MC/MD simulations refine fusion-property estimates by modeling atomic swaps and local-ordering effects on free-energy changes.
The integrated approach will produce melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change within roughly 5% of traditional methods.
The approach is broadly applicable to HEAs that form well-defined single-phase solid solutions.
Significant phase separation or complex intermetallic formation during melting reduces the applicability of the approach.
Prior DSC and CALPHAD evidence in binary and ternary systems supports the proposed HEA method.
High-temperature calibration challenges may introduce additional uncertainty.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims applicability across the high-entropy-alloy family, whereas the predicted outcome and boundary restrict reliable applicability mainly to single-phase solid solutions and acknowledge reduced applicability for phase-separating or intermetallic-forming alloys.
